content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Combine a symptom or need with a polite request for help. Model: “I feel dizzy, so could you call the clinic, please?” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use getting practical help clearly and politely. One useful response is: “I feel dizzy, so could you call the clinic, please?” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where getting practical help is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?
content_sections.title: Use it

exercises.prompt: Complete the natural sentence about getting practical help: I feel dizzy, so could you call the clinic, please?
Put these two parts in a natural order to make a message about getting practical help.
Make a short, personal response about getting practical help. Use the lesson language and add one detail that is yours.

criteria: The response communicates a clear meaning about getting practical help.
The response uses the allocated language in an understandable form.
The response adds an appropriate personal or invented detail.

language_focus: Combine a symptom or need with a polite request for help.
objectives: Combine a symptom or need with a polite request for help.
Use service-request integration in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about getting practical help.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about getting practical help. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: What does the speaker ask for?
listening.transcript: I feel sick. Could you help me call the clinic, please?

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Link could you; stress HELP and CLINIC. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Link could you; stress HELP and CLINIC.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about getting practical help.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using getting practical help; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise getting practical help?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: I feel dizzy, so could you call the clinic, please?

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about getting practical help with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about getting practical help. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: I feel dizzy, so could you call the clinic, please? Submit your draft first.
